candidates.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
candidates.abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{α,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_α^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $α$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^α$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $Λ_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_α^\infty\to\mathcal B^{α+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<α\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{α,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.

candidates.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
candidates.abstract: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.

candidates.title: A Robust Approach for Regression Analysis of Panel Count Data with Time-varying Covariates
candidates.comment: 35 pages, 1 figure in main text and 1 in appendix, 6 tables. Authors' accepted version of the article published in Bernoulli; includes the supplementary material as Appendices B-E
candidates.abstract: The validity of statistical inference for panel count data with time-varying covariates depends on the correct specification of within-subject correlation structures; misspecification often leads to questionable inference. To alleviate, robust inference has been proposed for mean models, which implicitly assume monotone mean functions. When covariate values fluctuate with time, however, the assumed monotonicity becomes unrealistic. In this research, we propose a robust inference based on rate models that are free of such constraints. Since the asymptotic variance has no closed form under the rate model, we further develop computationally efficient robust variance estimators using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, thus sidestepping the need for computationally intensive numerical methods, which could undermine the robustness. Rigorous theoretical development is provided in support of parameter estimation and inference. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method. We present a real clinical application to illustrate the use of the proposed method.

candidates.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
candidates.abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and étale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.

candidates.title: Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
candidates.abstract: We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. For three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. Below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. At and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. We also quantify the cost of control. The minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted Fourier norm of its periodised defect. For a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of Fourier degree at most $N$ grows linearly in $N$, i.e. Liouville ratios

candidates.title: An iterative procedure for statistical calibration
candidates.abstract: We study the iterative proportional fitting procedure (IPFP) under multiple pushforward constraints, motivated by model calibration. The goal is to find a distribution on model parameters whose pushforward by models matches data distributions. The classic convergence result of IPFP under marginal constraints establish convergence of IPFP under suitable regularity conditions and develop a variant of sequential importance sampling to approximate the iterative procedure. We also propose a related procedure for constructing a high probability parameter region. Simulation studies illustrate the performance of these methods. Finally, we apply IPFP to COVID19 ensemble forecasting. Variation of Covid strains across regions can lead to variation in surge rates and thus affect forecasting accuracy. To capture the variation, we estimate a probability distribution of epidemiological model parameters using early stage surge data from an ensemble of regions. We then propagate the distribution through the model to forecast both the ensemble's overall trend and its variability.

candidates.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
candidates.abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_θ$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<θ<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.

candidates.title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
candidates.abstract: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast i

candidates.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
candidates.abstract: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimesΛ_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenböck formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors

candidates.title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
candidates.abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchma

candidates.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
candidates.abstract: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$. When $Y$ is dismantlable, we show that the boundary isomorphism assumption can be weakened to a bijection between the vertex sets of both boundaries with an additional technical condition on boundary edges.

candidates.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
candidates.abstract: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erdős--Rényi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $Θ(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit

candidates.title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
candidates.abstract: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists. We then determine the structure of singular solutions. Outside $N$ every pole is simple, with residue $-1$, and is not a Darboux surface; along non-characteristic factors of $N$ the leading polar coefficient is free Cauchy data; and the only unknown denominator is a squarefree polynomial $D$, which enters a linear equation. A Newton-polygon analysis at infinity gives the polynomial part up to a correction of bounded weight. The weighted degree of $D$ is determined exactly when the excess is zero and the top Riccati equation has no algebraic solution, and is bounded by residues of the top field otherwise, conditionally on the vanishing of that c

candidates.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, Hà, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. candidates.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
candidates.abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

candidates.title: A singular Lawson cone minimizing the fractional perimeter in dimension seven
candidates.abstract: We prove that the nonlocal Lawson cone constructed by Davila, del Pino, and Wei (J. Differential Geom. 2018) in $N=7$ minimizes the fractional perimeter for all sufficiently small orders $s$. Thus nonlocal minimal surfaces can have singularities already in dimension $7$. This contrasts both with the classical theory, where the first singular example occurs in dimension $8$ (Bombieri-De Giorgi-Giusti, Invent. Math. 1969), and with the fractional theory for orders $s$ close to $1$ (Caffarelli-Valdinoci, Adv. Math. 2013).

candidates.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
candidates.abstract: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.

candidates.title: Estimation for High-Dimensional Hawkes Processes with Inhibition via CIR Approximation
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we develop a parametric estimation method for a high-dimensional Hawkes processes with inhibition. The proposed approach relies on a quantitative approximation of the Hawkes process by a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the joint large-population and long-time regime. This result requires specific techniques to handle the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient of the limiting CIR process.Based on this approximation, we construct explicit and easily implementable estimators of the model parameters. We establish their consistency and asymptotic normality. We also conduct numerical experiments to illustrate our findings.

candidates.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
candidates.abstract: We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$. As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$). As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for foliations of constant mean curvature embedded hypersurfaces near a stable minimal surface. The resulting foliation supplies nonlocal barriers thanks to known results of uniform convergence of the nonlocal mean curvature to the classical one when $s \to 1$.

candidates.title: Global dynamics of impulsive reaction-diffusion systems with asymptotically unbounded domain
candidates.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the global dynamics of continuous-discrete hybrid population models with an asymptotically unbounded domain. We first prove a global attractivity result for a class of impulsive reaction-diffusion equations whose diffusion coefficients vanish asymptotically. A cut-off function is combined with an auxiliary impulsive kinetic system to construct a subsolution that is compatible with the birth update at every cycle. We then use comparison arguments to establish threshold-type dynamics for the original model when the birth function is either monotone or nonmonotone. It turns out that the threshold value for extinction and persistence is explicitly determined by the birth pulse, the within-cycle growth, and the asymptotic expansion rate of the habitat.

candidates.title: Functional Direct Binomial Regression for Right-Censored Competing Risks Data
candidates.abstract: Existing regression-based methods for functional predictors often overlook right-censored competing risks outcomes, limiting their applicability in many biomedical studies. To address this gap, this article proposes a functional direct binomial model for right-censored competing risks data, where a binary outcome indicates the occurrence of an event of interest before a fixed time horizon. The model enables straightforward prediction of the cumulative incidence function, can be fitted using standard, scalable algorithms for large-scale studies, and has broad applications to functional predictors, such as wearable device data. We establish large-sample theory to facilitate inference, including hypothesis testing and the construction of confidence intervals and bands for both scalar coefficients and functional parameters. The methodology is further extended to accommodate multiple functional biomarkers and to handle missing failure causes. Simulation studies confirm that the proposed method provides accurate estimation and valid inference. We illustrate the approach with an application to modeling time to advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) in the presence of the competing risk of

candidates.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
candidates.abstract: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities. It distinguishes triangles supported by a common group from those requiring three distinct groups. Second, explicit representations of global and average local clustering reveal their different dependence on model parameters and the role of shared groups in edge correlations. Finally, by varying the strength and spatial range of group memberships, we establish convergence to random connection, random geometric, random intersection, Erdős--Rényi, and complete graphs. We characterize the corresponding clustering limits and show that clustering need not converge to that of the limiting graph, highlighting the distinction between spatially local convergence and global graph statistics.

candidates.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
candidates.abstract: We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations. As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.

candidates.title: Mortgage Backed Securities with p-Laplacian Diffusion and Random Prepayment
candidates.abstract: In this note we consider deterministic and stochastic versions of a PDE pricing model for mortgage backed securities, driven by p-Laplacian motion. We show the existence of weak solutions in the $1<p<2$ case, for sufficiently small initial data. In the stochastic case, we consider a random prepayment function, when $p=2$. Herein we derive results concerning the uniform first order sensitivity and mean squared sensitivity of the solution, to the pricing model.

candidates.title: Error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems
candidates.abstract: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the convergence of the scheme and indicate second-order convergence in space in the $L^2$ norm.

candidates.title: Horseshoe-Type Shrinkage from Ratio-Generated Priors
candidates.abstract: We develop a class of horseshoe-type shrinkage priors generated by ratios of independent numerator and denominator random variables. Large denominator values produce concentration near zero, small denominator values generate heavy tails, and the numerator determines scale and geometry and may also influence tail behavior. We establish general origin and tail asymptotics, including power and logarithmic singularities. Under a Gaussian likelihood and regularly varying prior tails, the posterior mean approaches the observation for large signals, with risk approaching that of the unshrunk observation. The denominator also induces a latent shrinkage factor. For a Cauchy denominator, this factor has exactly the ${\rm Beta}(1/2,1/2)$ distribution, whatever the numerator. With a Gaussian numerator and appropriate scale calibration, it recovers the classical horseshoe shrinkage coefficient, whereas non-Gaussian numerators can change the effective posterior shrinkage, even in its asymptotic rate. The Cauchy/Cauchy prior illustrates the theory, with a logarithmic singularity at the origin in one dimension, power singularities in higher dimensions, and logarithmically modified Cauchy-order tai

candidates.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
candidates.comment: The mathematics in this article was developed by the authors without the use of AI
candidates.abstract: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.

candidates.title: Cooperative colorings of cycles and uniform cycle factors
candidates.abstract: A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring. Together with known bounds, this determines, for every $\ell\geq3$, the least number $m$ such that every $m$ graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, have a cooperative coloring. For $\ell\geq3$, this number is four when $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ and three otherwise. These results answer two questions of Aharoni, Holzman, Howard, and Sprüssel.

candidates.title: The hitting time index: bounds, a sharp threshold, the proof of a conjecture and the disproof of another conjecture
candidates.abstract: We prove some new upper and lower bounds for the hitting time index ($HT$ index) of an $n$-vertex graph, showing along the way that the largest order of the index is $n^5$ and the smallest is $n^3$. More specifically, we prove the conjecture that the smallest value of the index is $\frac{n(n-1)^2}{2}$, which is attained by the complete graph. We also find a sharp threshold for the minimal degree $δ$ so that the $HT$ index goes from an $n^4$ order to an $n^3$ order if the threshold is surpassed. We disprove the conjecture that the largest value of the index is attained by the $n$-path, and look at the lollipop graphs, some of which attain the $n^5$ order, and seem to be the natural candidates among which the largest value of the index should be attained.

candidates.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras
candidates.abstract: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

candidates.title: Global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional Zhidkov space
candidates.abstract: We show global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the Zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. For the usual nonlinear Schrödinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. Here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. Global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+H^1$ follows. We also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to different nonlinearities.

candidates.title: Degree-respecting labellings with ordered neighbour sums
candidates.abstract: In an exhaustive enumeration of hydrocarbons with only single bonds, carbon skeletons are generated as adjacency matrices and pruned by two rules: a vertex of larger degree receives a smaller label, and among vertices of equal degree, a vertex whose adjacency row is the larger binary integer receives a smaller label. The pruning is sound only if every skeleton admits a labelling obeying both rules. We prove that such a labelling exists for every finite simple graph, connected or not and with no bound on the degrees, and that the same holds when the weights $2^i$ of the labels $i$ are replaced by any strictly increasing real weights. The proof takes, among the labellings that order vertices by non-increasing degree, one minimising the sum over edges of the products of the endpoint weights.

candidates.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
candidates.abstract: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. A GPU-based finite-difference implementation, released as an open-source Python library, achieves speedups greater than x30 for realistic mesh sizes, making three-dimensional simulations on realistic geometries computationally tractable. This provides a basis for future in-silico studies of treatment strategies, such as testing antiviral or immunomodulatory therapies, and for patient-specific simulations based on individual liver geometries, paving the way towards personalized healthcare.

candidates.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
candidates.abstract: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

candidates.title: A square analogue of the diamond order and a unified approach to the plus order
candidates.abstract: We introduce the square order $\le^\square$ on group invertible matrices, defined by $A^3=ABA$ and $A\le^s B$, where $\le^s$ is the space pre-order. It is the group inverse analogue of the diamond order: $A\le^\square B$ if and only if $A^\#\le^- B^\#$. Using its block representation, we characterize the reverse order law $(AB)^\#=B^\#A^\#$ for $A\le^\square B$. In contrast to the Moore--Penrose case, the conditions $A\le^- B$ and $(B-A)^\#=B^\#-A^\#$ do not characterize the sharp order; instead, they lead to new partial orders between the sharp and square orders. We also develop a framework where the plus order replaces the minus order in Mitra's unified theory. For a map $\mathcal G$ assigning to each matrix $A$ a subset of its inner inverses, we define $A\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A=PBQ$ for some pair $(P,Q)=(AA^-,A^-A)$, $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$, whereas Mitra's relation requires $A=PB=BQ$, and $A\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A^-\le^-B^-$ for some reflexive $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$ and $B^-\in\mathcal G(B)$. When $\mathcal G(A)$ consists of a single reflexive inverse, we characterize the transitivity of $\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}$ in terms of $\preceq^{\math

candidates.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
candidates.abstract: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

candidates.title: Polynomial-degree-robust saturation on triangular meshes
candidates.abstract: We prove a polynomial-degree-robust ($p$-robust) saturation property for conforming finite element approximations of the Poisson equation on shape-regular triangular meshes. Previously, a $p$-robust saturation estimate for the spectral method on a square was proved in [C. Canuto et al., A saturation property for the spectral-Galerkin approximation of a Dirichlet problem in a square, ESAIM Math. Model. Numer. Anal., 53 (2019), pp. 987--1003]. For every fixed $λ>1$, increasing the polynomial degree from $p$ to any $q\geq\lceilλp\rceil+3$ reduces the energy error by a factor $α_λ\in(0,1)$ independent of $p$ and the mesh size, up to a data oscillation term.

candidates.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.

candidates.title: Weak-strong stability and uniqueness of measure-valued solutions to (nonlocal) pressureless Euler-type systems
candidates.abstract: We consider the pressureless Euler equation possibly coupled with non-local forces like the Poisson and alignment interactions. We overcome the lack of strict convexity in the relative entropy inequality that arises from the lack of pressure. The key to this result is the appropriate framework of the solution scheme utilizing the generalized Young measure which yields extra structural properties for the oscillation and concentration parts of the measure-valued solution. We overcome the problem of density mismatch via two complementary techniques. The first takes advantage of a Figalli--Kang-type transport inequality. The second involves establishing a generation lemma for the generalized Young measure which simultaneously establishes $L^2$-based control in flat metric between the measure-valued density and the density generating sequence.

candidates.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
candidates.abstract: For a polynomial map $φ\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $φ^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $dφ$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $φ$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set. These results apply to every counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture and to families of Keller maps. For the explicit three-dimensional counterexample we show that $\A^3$ is the variety of binary cubic forms of a special shape with a marked simple root, and that $F$ forgets the root. This gives the degree, the fibres, the non-properness set, the monodromy and the structure of the twisted ternary algebra. Three examples modelled on weighted scrolls illustrate equivariance, degeneration to an automorphism, and an $A_1$ singularity of the fibre.

candidates.title: The capillary $L_{p}$ dual Christoffel-Minkowski-type problem for $p\geq q$ with $1\leq k\leq n$
candidates.abstract:
We study the following fully nonlinear $k$-Hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_θ$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<θ<π/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} σ_k(

In the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $C^0$ estimates without normalization. We overcome this difficulty using a logarithmic gradient estimate and a normalized approximation with uniqueness up to dilation.

candidates.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
candidates.abstract: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.

candidates.title: Veronese Classification of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics
candidates.abstract: We prove that every linearly full, irreducible conformal minimal immersion of constant Gaussian curvature and finite isotropy order from the two-sphere into a complex hyperquadric comes from a member of a Veronese sequence. The result holds at every finite isotropy order, without an unramifiedness or additional Frenet-norm polynomiality assumption. Both the associated projective harmonic sequence and the target harmonic sequence are totally unramified as consequences. If the replacement depth is \(\ell\) and the holomorphic seed spans \(\mathbb{CP}^m\), the curvature is \(K=2/((2\ell+1)m-2\ell^2)\) in the Grassmannian normalization. Real Gram data characterize the admissible embeddings and give an algebraic converse. The proof uses holomorphic Pfaffian norm identities, degree estimates that retain all ramification divisors, and a valuation argument that identifies the retained lines with seed Frenet lines.

candidates.title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
candidates.abstract: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,μ)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,μ)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.

candidates.title: Rigidity of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics at Isotropy Order $n-6$
candidates.abstract: We classify linearly full, irreducible, totally unramified conformal minimal two-spheres of constant Gaussian curvature in the real Grassmannian $G(2,n;\mathbb R)$, or equivalently in the complex hyperquadric $Q_{n-2}$, whose finite isotropy order is $n-6$, where $n\geq7$. We remove the additional polynomiality assumption on a Frenet norm in the earlier classification of Li and Jiao. An exterior-product norm identity reduces the problem to the multiplicity of the irreducible polynomial $1+zw$; a further divisibility argument handles the boundary dimension $n=7$, including isotropy order one. The dimension $n$ is necessarily odd, and the immersion is congruent, after a conformal reparametrization, to the second member of a Veronese sequence with its prescribed real structure. Its curvature is $2/(5n-13)$ in the Grassmannian normalization. An explicit model in $Q_5$ illustrates the boundary case and its harmonic sequence.

candidates.title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
candidates.abstract: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $ν^{es}\otimesν^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

candidates.title: Two-type thinning with alternative leader rate for random partition structures
candidates.abstract: A dust-free random partition structure with infinitely many parts is a random sequence $(\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots)$ with $\mathsf{X}_1>\mathsf{X}_2>\dots>0$ such that $\mathsf{X}_1+\mathsf{X}_2+\dots=1$, almost surely. The Poisson-Dirichlet $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ distributions for $0<m<1$ are defined such that $\mathsf{X}_n = ξ_n^{-1/m}/\sum_{ν=1}^{\infty} ξ_ν^{-1/m}$, where $0<ξ_1<ξ_2<\dots$ is a homogeneous Poisson point process. It is a model for thinning invariant random partition structures, where every one of the infinitely many parts $\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots$ are thinned IID at rate 1. We consider a 2-type thinning where the instantaneous leader is deleted with an alternative rate $1+r\geq 0$. Then we seek time stationary random partition structures. When $r =R\in \{0,1,\dots\}$ a solution is obtained by taking $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ and performing ``balayage,'' where balayage means simply excavating the first $R$ points. We find the solutions for all $r \in (-1,\infty)$, which we call $\mathrm{PD}^{(r)}(m,0)$. We motivate with an application, and we present graphical representations.

candidates.title: Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension
candidates.abstract: We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions. We give examples in both the measure-theoretic and topological senses, showing that this entropy gap condition is sharp. We also present applications related to the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps.

candidates.title: The modulus of smoothness and \(\ell_p\)-generation
candidates.abstract: Fabian, Godefroy, Hájek and Zizler [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{200} (2003), 301--323, Theorem~2] proved that at density \(\aleph_1\), generation by a space whose modulus of smoothness has power type \(p\), \(1<p\le 2\), is equivalent to \(\ell_p(Γ)\)-generation. We extend this equivalence to arbitrary density, with \(|Γ|=\dens X\), answering \mbox{Problem~291} of Guirao, Montesinos and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~127]. The proof combines an upper \(\ell_p\)-estimate on successive projection differences with transfinite induction on density. We characterize generation by superreflexive spaces and by their \(\ell_2\)-sums, and obtain \(\ell_{\min\{r,2\}}\)-generation for closed subspaces of \(L^r(μ)\), \(1<r<\infty\), including Hilbert generation for \(r\ge 2\).

candidates.title: Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals
candidates.abstract: Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

candidates.title: Counting complex elliptic curves with self-quotients via class numbers
candidates.abstract: Let \(n>1\) be an integer. We consider complex elliptic curves \(E\) admitting a finite subgroup \(C\subset E(\mathbb C)\) of order \(n\) such that \(E/C\) is isomorphic to \(E\). % with the additional requirement that the invariant factors of (C) are unequal. We establish class-number counting formulas for the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases. More precisely, we associate to every negative quadratic-order discriminant \(D\) the norm form \[ Q_D(x,y)=x^2+\varepsilon_Dxy+q_Dy^2, \] where \[ \varepsilon_D\in\{0,1\},\qquad q_D=\frac{\varepsilon_D^2-D}{4}. \] The invariant factors of the kernel of the corresponding endomorphism are determined by \(\gcd(x,y)\). This leads to finite sets of admissible discriminants describing the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases with unequal invariant factors. Our main result expresses the numbers of isomorphism classes in the three cases as sums of the proper ideal class numbers \(h(D)\) over explicitly defined finite sets of admissible discriminants. This provides an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work by \cite{CanepaGaba2014,CanepaGaba2019,CanepaGabaOlteanu2022} and its subsequent alg

candidates.title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics
candidates.abstract: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.

candidates.title: From Limit Theorems to Mixing Limit Theorems
candidates.abstract: Following the work of Gouëzel, we give an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of a result of Arana-Herrera and Forni, which provides a general method for upgrading limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems to mixing limit theorems.

candidates.title: Random walk on an induced component of the uniform spanning forest
candidates.abstract: Let $T$ be the component of the origin in the uniform spanning forest of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and consider the induced graph $H$ obtained by retaining every lattice edge with both endpoints in $T$. Lyons, Peres and Sun (2020) showed that $H$ is recurrent if $d \ge 8$ and asked for which $d \in \{5,6,7\}$ this holds. We prove that simple random walk on $H$ is transient for $d=5$ and recurrent for every $d\ge6$. We also show that the quenched return probabilities to the origin satisfy $p^H_{2n}(o,o)=n^{-α_d+o(1)}$ a.s., where $α_5=4/3$ and $α_6=1$, while $α_7=4/5$ and $α_d=2/3$ for all $d\ge8$.

candidates.title: On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$
candidates.abstract: The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $Γ(Ω,q)$, where $Ω$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix. We then derive several significant properties regarding the symmetry, connectivity and girth of $Γ(Ω,q)$. For arbitrary nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, we fully characterize the connected components of $Γ(Ω_{m,n},q)$, which is isomorphic to a canonical projection of $D(k,q)$ with $k\geq 2m+2$. Our results demonstrate that the connected components of $\{Γ(Ω_{m,n},q)\}_{2\leq |m-n|\leq 3}$ form a novel family of graphs with large girth in the sense of Biggs.

candidates.title: Exact Integration of ReLU-type Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
candidates.abstract: Developing robust training methodologies for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with neural networks is crucial for reliable scientific computing. Piecewise-linear activations such as the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) are a convenient choice in this setting as their structure resembles classical piecewise-linear approximations. However, when the loss functional incorporates the spatial gradient of the network, as in the Deep Ritz method, numerical integration becomes problematic. Specifically, relying on standard integration techniques (e.g., Monte Carlo sampling) during training yields incorrect gradients, even as the number of integration points approaches infinity, leading to optimization failure. To overcome this limitation, we present an integration framework for single-hidden-layer ReLU networks that computes correct gradients when using Deep Ritz for PDEs or PINNs for first-order problems. Our approach employs the Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm to partition the physical domain into subdomains according to breaking hyperplanes underlying the ReLU network. By finding these hyperplanes exactly, our method can correctly integrate the gradients, ensuring the optimizer rec

candidates.title: Nonradial asymptotic stability of radial steady states for the viscous vector Burgers equation in an exterior domain with positive far field
candidates.abstract: We study the viscous vector Burgers equation outside a ball in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, near a radial stationary state with positive far-field value. For every fixed $b,μ,r_0>0$, we prove global existence and $L^\infty$ asymptotic stability for continuous, nonradial vector perturbations that vanish at infinity, satisfy the homogeneous boundary condition, and are small only in $L^\infty$. The perturbations need not be irrotational or integrable, and no initial-gradient assumption is imposed. A Bessel-weight conjugation and a divergence--curl identity yield weighted coercivity. A moving-front argument, a stopped stochastic estimate for angular momentum, and scalar Burgers comparison then recover convergence in the physical supremum norm. We also establish a quantitative Lyapunov estimate and, for perturbations compactly supported in the radial variable, an $O(t^{-1/4})$ decay bound. No additional restriction on the dimensionless parameter $br_0/μ$ is required.

candidates.title: Spectral stability and nonlinear asymptotics of radial steady states for the viscous vector Burgers equation in an exterior domain with negative far field
candidates.abstract: We study radial stationary waves of the multidimensional viscous vector Burgers equation in the exterior of a ball, with strictly negative radial far-field data. For each fixed wave satisfying a strict modified-Bessel admissibility criterion, a positive-weight conjugation yields a self-adjoint linearized operator with a positive isolated lowest eigenvalue below its essential spectrum. We establish global nonlinear stability under general continuous vector perturbations that are small in a mixed weighted-$L^2$ and unweighted-$L^\infty$ norm, without requiring small initial gradients or compact support. The lowest-eigenvalue exponential decay rate is attained for a nonempty class of admissible data. We further identify the nonlinear lowest-mode amplitude and derive refined weighted-$L^2$ and physical-variable $L^\infty$ remainder estimates, including the possible resonant case, together with a quadratic expansion in the initial data with a uniform cubic remainder.

candidates.title: The asymptotics of maximal rank of three-way tensors
candidates.abstract: We prove that the maximal rank of an $n\times n\times n$ tensor is $n^2/3+O(n^{3/2})$, over the real numbers and over every algebraically closed field. More generally, in format $\lfloor an\rfloor\times\lfloor bn\rfloor\times\lfloor cn\rfloor$, with $a,b,c>0$ fixed, the leading term is $\frac{abc}{a+b+c}n^2$. The argument starts with a criterion for rank with respect to an arbitrary projective variety: a decomposition of zero with surjective differential, from a smooth parameter space, bounds the rank of every point. For Segre varieties, we construct such decompositions using a basis of units in a split algebra. We also give an optimized finite bound and a closed estimate with explicit constants for the maximal rank.

candidates.title: Existence and nonexistence results for a mixed local--nonlocal operator with a Hardy potential
candidates.abstract: We investigate a class of problems involving the mixed local-nonlocal operator $-Δ+(-Δ)^s$, with $s\in(0,1)$, and a Hardy-type potential, in a bounded smooth domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\geq 3$, containing the origin. The problem involves a positive parameter $λ$ and a nonnegative measurable function $f$ satisfying suitable assumptions. We first study the associated linear problem with a prescribed datum. By means of a suitable change of variables and within an appropriate framework of weighted Sobolev spaces, we establish a weak Harnack inequality for the resulting weighted mixed operator. As a consequence, we derive the precise asymptotic behavior of nonnegative solutions near the singularity at the origin, and we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of weak solutions. We then address the nonlinear case for two classes of nonlinearities, namely $f(x,u)=u^q+g(x)$ and $f(x,u)=h(x)/u^σ$. For the first class, we identify a critical exponent governing the existence of solutions; for the second, we establish existence results for a broad class of data $h$.

candidates.title: The Exact Nef-Curve Cone Formula for dlt Pairs
candidates.abstract: We prove an exact rational-curve formula for the nef-curve cone of every complex projective dlt pair with effective real boundary, answering the related question proposed by Cascini. Every $(K_X+Δ)$-negative extremal ray is generated by a movable rational curve whose normalization is free in the smooth locus. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.

candidates.title: On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field
candidates.abstract: Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $Σ$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.

candidates.title: Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
candidates.abstract: We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal diffeomorphism directions, and give explicit self-similar flows. The normalized Ricci-flow velocity is an admissible Chen-Nagano variation for n > = 3, and the smooth Poincar'e theorem admits an equivalent formulation in terms of the existence of harmonic critical metrics

candidates.title: Lower deviations for the maximum of a branching random walk in a random environment in time: quenched versus annealed
candidates.comment: 21 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to Journal of Theoretical Probability. Code and numerical data are provided as ancillary files
candidates.abstract: We study lower deviations of the rightmost position in a supercritical branching random walk whose offspring laws are independent and identically distributed across generations. Every particle has at least one child, and displacements have a fixed law with finite exponential moments of all orders. For thresholds strictly between the lower endpoint of the step law and the speed of the maximum, the quenched lower deviation probability has a finite positive exponential rate precisely when the negative logarithm of the probability of a single child is integrable. We identify the rate by a variational formula. If a positive fraction of generations rule out single children and displacements are bounded below, the probability decays doubly exponentially. We compute its double-exponential rate in terms of the minimum offspring numbers, the lower endpoint of the displacement law, and the speed of the maximum. After averaging over the environment, the negative logarithm of the probability is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the generation number whenever single children are possible with positive probability. We obtain the exact exponential rate when the offspring mean is con

candidates.title: Conjugation-preserving polynomial and rational interpolation for limited-memory matrix-function actions
candidates.abstract: Approximating $f(A)b$ for a large nonsymmetric matrix can require substantial storage if a long Krylov basis is retained. We develop polynomial and rational interpolation schemes that use a fixed number of large recurrence vectors and preserve conjugation symmetry. Starting from a prescribed scalar approximation region, the schemes organize real nodes and complex-conjugate pairs into Newton-like bases with real interpolation coefficients. The polynomial and single-real-pole recurrences use real arithmetic in the matrix-action stage; the multi-pole construction also exploits conjugate pole pairs. A conjugation-preserving AAA procedure supplies interpolation data for the latter. We establish the interpolation and basis properties and compare the resulting realizations with Leja, Taylor, and Krylov methods on matrices from differential equations, model reduction, and networks. The experiments demonstrate arithmetic savings relative to complex-arithmetic counterparts and identify the influence of shifted solves and orthogonalization requirements. The methods are intended for memory-constrained computations in which useful approximation-region information is available.

candidates.title: Model and higher-order structure-preserving scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we study the model and higher-order structure-preserving numerical scheme for the chemotaxis equations modeling the growth of bacterial colonies. By using a new variational analysis method, we first rigidly derive the nonnegativity for two solutions of the chemotaxis equations. Then, utilizing the finite element method with mass-lumping in space and the BDF scheme with the positivity-preserving extrapolation to deal with the nonlinear terms in time, we propose a high-order fully discrete framework for the chemotaxis equations by combining with the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) shift and the Lagrange multiplier method, which preserves the mass conservation of the discrete system and the nonnegativity of two approximation solutions. Moreover, apart from confirming the existence and uniqueness of the nonlinear equation generated by the Lagrange multiplier method, by classifying its structure in detail, we prove that the secant iteration method for this nonlinear equation is locally convergent. Finally, we show some experiments to verify the theoretical prediction and efficiency of the proposed scheme, including consistent simulations of the growth of the colonies under diffe

candidates.title: Geometric realization of the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in a partially ramified case
candidates.abstract: We construct a new family of algebraic varieties over a finite field, realizing the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in their compactly supported étale cohomology. The resulting representations have $L$-parameters which are induced from characters of a partially ramified field extension.

candidates.title: Kelvin-invariant positive solutions for critical elliptic systems with repulsive interaction
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we consider the following critical nonlinear elliptic system with repulsive interaction: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δu_1 = μ_1 u_1^3 - β(x) u_1 u_2^2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr -Δu_2 = μ_2 u_2^3 - β(x) u_1^2 u_2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr u_1, u_2 \in \mathcal{D}^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^4), & \end{array} \right. \] where $μ_1, μ_2 > 0$ and $β(x) \in C(\mathbb{R}^4,\mathbb{R})$ is a nonnegative function. Assuming that $β$ is invariant under the map $x \mapsto -\frac{x}{\vert{}x\vert{}^2}$, we establish the existence of positive solutions to $(\mathcal{P}_β)$ that are invariant under the Kelvin transform subject to suitable assumptions. This result provides a critical counterpart to the work of Sato [Y. Sato, Nonlinear Anal. 234 (2023), 113302], who established the existence of an even ground state for the corresponding subcritical problem. Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the obtained solutions as $\|β\|_\infty \to 0$.

candidates.title: Policy and Value Iteration for Entropy-Regularized Stochastic Control
candidates.abstract: We study finite-horizon entropy-regularized stochastic control with action-independent diffusion. To solve the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, we alternate between value and policy updates. Each iteration approximately solves a linear backward equation for the current policy, then approximates the Gibbs distribution defined by the resulting value gradient. We prove a uniform bound on the final policy's excess regularized cost. The bound assigns explicit, summable weights to the evaluation residuals and the Kullback-Leibler divergences from the updated policies to their Gibbs targets. Under the stated assumptions and with exact terminal data, vanishing errors in both steps imply uniform convergence to the optimal value. Two finite-horizon execution problems test value accuracy against a known solution and closed-loop performance when no exact solution is available. We also evaluate the iteration on a discounted infinite-horizon routing problem with twelve modes and an unregularized HJB benchmark in up to 10,000 dimensions.

candidates.title: Fixed-level profiles and fluctuations in age-dependent recursive trees
candidates.abstract: How many vertices of a growing recursive tree lie at a prescribed distance from the root? We compare two linear attachment rules. When an arriving vertex chooses a parent with probability proportional to its label, each fixed level eventually stops growing. We determine the limiting covariance kernel and the probability that a level will change again after time $n$. Writing $L_\infty(h)$ for its final size, we show that $2^{-h}L_\infty(h)$ converges in mean square as $h$ tends to infinity to a random variable with mean $1$ and variance $1/3$. Consequently the limiting variance of the level size is asymptotic to $4^h/3$. When parents are chosen with probability proportional to their age, each fixed level grows. Its centered fluctuations have a joint Gaussian limit whose covariance constants come from repeated logarithmic integration of attachment noise at the root. An exact finite-size calculation illustrates the difference between the limiting and finite-size variances.

candidates.title: Duality of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions via inclusions
candidates.abstract: We study actions of finite-dimensional Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras on a unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$. We first define the Rokhlin property and approximate representability directly for an action $H\curvearrowright A$ and characterize these properties, under appropriate hypotheses, in terms of the corresponding properties of the canonical conditional expectation $E\colon A\to A^H$. Based on this characterization, we establish the following duality for a saturated action on a simple unital $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra $A$ such that $A\rtimes H$ is simple: 1. $H\curvearrowright A$ has the Rokhlin property if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ is approximately representable. 2. $H\curvearrowright A$ is approximately representable if and only if the dual action $H^{\circ}\curvearrowright A\rtimes H$ has the Rokhlin property. For separable $A$, we also identify these properties with the corresponding spatial formulations introduced by Barlak--Szab{ó}--Voigt, assuming saturation in the Rokhlin comparison. We present examples of Hopf $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra actions both with and without the Rokhlin property.

candidates.title: Total Curvature and Topology of Complete Euclidean Immersions: Heat Kernel and Boundary Morse Approaches
candidates.abstract: Two mechanisms relate the scale-invariant integral of the second fundamental form to topology at infinity of a complete Euclidean immersion. The first retains the mean-curvature potential in the Michael--Simon Sobolev inequality, establishes an ultracontractive estimate for the semigroup generated by $Δ+|H|^2$, and uses a vector-bundle Cwikel--Lieb--Rozenblum bound to estimate spaces of $L^2$-harmonic forms. Together with the theory of nonparabolic ends, this yields $e(M)\le 1+C_n\int_M|A|^n$ for arbitrary complete immersed $n$-manifolds, $n\ge3$. The second method, under the additional assumption of finitely many single-sheeted $C^2$-asymptotically planar graphical ends, uses a boundary Morse complex and the normal Gauss-map area formula to prove $\sum_j b_j(M;\F)+e(M)-2\le\TA(F)$. It supplies an explicit end coefficient and bounds ordinary Betti numbers. We provide proofs of both mechanisms, identify the exact role of their respective hypotheses, and discuss minimal and Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian specializations.

candidates.title: Necessary conditions for the boundedness of directional maximal operators
candidates.abstract: Given a set of directions $Ω$, we investigate whether the associated directional maximal operator $M\_Ω$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$, for $p>1$. One can associate to $Ω$ a numerical quantity called its \textit{Perron capacity}. If the latter is finite, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for $p \geq 1$. In this paper, we generalize a method introduced by D'Aniello, Gauvan and Moonens to compute the Perron capacity of oscillatory sets of directions such as \[ Ω\_{\mathrm{cos}} = \left \{\frac{\cos (n)}{n}\,: n \in \NN^*\right \}. \] In a second part, using geometric arguments, we show that if the Minkowski dimension of $Ω$ is positive, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for a small range of $p>1$.

candidates.title: The irreducibility of tame character varieties
candidates.abstract: Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.

candidates.title: Multiple positive solutions near segregated profiles in Lotka-Volterra competition systems with asymmetric interactions
candidates.abstract: We consider stationary Lotka--Volterra competition-diffusion systems with any number of species and positive, possibly asymmetric competition coefficients. We study two settings with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions: a one-dimensional interval with constant drift, and radial solutions on a ball. In each setting we first determine when a prescribed ordering of species admits a segregated profile. Starting from such a profile, we construct a positive solution for every sufficiently large competition parameter $β$. The uniform distance from the profile is of order $\varepsilon=β^{-1/3}$, and the rescaled densities converge near each interface to a two-species model. Counting the admissible orderings gives a lower bound on the number of positive solutions. We also prove a non-approximation result when one directed competition coefficient is zero and the other species are suppressed on the interval or shell used in the proof.

candidates.title: Global existence of small data solutions to 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations, II
candidates.abstract: For the 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation $\square u+\fracμ{t}\partial_tu=|u|^p$, where $t\geq1$, $μ>0$ and $p>1$, it is conjectured that the small data solution $u$ exists globally when $p>p_s(3+μ)=\frac{μ+4+\sqrt{μ^2+16μ+32}}{2(μ+2)}$ for $0<μ\le \frac{14}{5}$, and when $p>p_f(3)=\frac{5}{3}$ for $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, where $p_s$ and $p_f$ denote the Strauss and Fujita exponents, respectively. In our previous paper [Li Qianqian, Yin Huicheng, Global existence of small data solutions to 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations. Preprint (2026), arXiv:2607.04575], for $p>\max\{\frac{5}{3},1+\frac{2}μ\}$ and $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, the global small solution $u$ was obtained. In this paper, we establish the global existence of $u$ for the remaining range of $\frac{5}{3}<p\leq1+\frac{2}μ$ and $μ\ge \frac{14}{5}$. Therefore, the above 3-D conjecture for $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$ is solved.

candidates.title: Scattering for the defocusing two-dimensional NLS with an Aharonov-Bohm magnetic potential
candidates.abstract: We study the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in two dimensions in the presence of an Aharonov--Bohm magnetic potential with noninteger flux. Working with the Friedrichs realization of the magnetic Hamiltonian, we establish global well-posedness for initial data in the weighted magnetic energy space. For mass-critical and mass-supercritical nonlinearities, we prove convergence of the interaction representation in the same weighted space, while in the mass-subcritical range we obtain scattering in the magnetic energy space. The proof is based on a magnetic lens transformation, which converts the original equation into a nonlinear equation governed by the Aharonov--Bohm harmonic oscillator on a finite time interval. Existence is obtained through truncation, compactness, and energy estimates, whereas uniqueness follows directly from the dispersive decay of the confined linear flow. This approach avoids derivative Strichartz estimates, which are delicate in the presence of the singular magnetic field.

candidates.title: On Shepp's property in free probability
candidates.abstract: We establish a free analogue of Shepp's theorem for freely independent standard semicircular elements. We show more generally that a family of self-normalized squared quadratic forms is free, and each has a standard Marchenko-Pastur distribution. The free analogue of Shepp's theorem follows by taking the coefficients of quadratic forms to be the three Pauli matrices. We also prove some new free analogues of Lukacs-type independence results. The key part of the proof is a construction of an equivalent and simpler operator model on a corner algebra compressed by a free projection.

candidates.title: $99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point
candidates.abstract: When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.
